subject: Cluster performance envelope & scaling playbook — initial traffic profiles
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: alice.wu@cobalt.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Cluster performance envelope & scaling playbook — initial traffic profiles

Hi Alice / Cobalt infra team,

Thanks for the sync earlier. Following up with the traffic export and a few concrete asks so we can draft a scaling playbook for your private GPU pool (VPC). Attached: traffic_profile_v2.csv which is a 14-day sample of request arrival rates grouped by tenant and route.

High-level asks from our side:
- Can you confirm the sustained 95th percentile QPS per route during your peak windows (09:00–11:00 and 20:00–22:00 local)?
- Target latency SLOs: are you aiming for 99th p50/p95/p99 buckets? If you have a P99 target we should plan warm pool sizing accordingly.
- Any hard constraints on egress (GB/hr) or burstable NIC quotas?

What we propose next:
1) We’ll draft a "performance envelope" that maps traffic quantiles to GPU pool sizes and warm pool keep-alive rules.
2) Internal ops (Jonas + Marissa) will validate kernel/tiling assumptions and warmup time constants.
3) Schedule a 30-min runbook review on Friday to finalize scaling thresholds.

Attachments: [Attachment: traffic_profile_v2.csv (CSV, 48KB)]

Why this matters in plain terms — we want to avoid two failure modes: underprovisioning (queueing spikes and P99 regressions) and overprovisioning (excess commit and idle cost). The playbook will include graduated scale steps, a fast-failover model to a smaller-latency model variant, and a short warm-up choreography.

Can you respond with the QPS quantiles and any network egress limits by EOD tomorrow? Once we have those numbers Jonas will run a simulation and Marissa will draft the playbook skeleton.

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

From: Alice Wu <alice.wu@cobalt.ai>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: ops@cobalt.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-16T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Cluster performance envelope & scaling playbook — initial traffic profiles

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and the CSV. A few quick answers pulled from our telemetry:
- Peak windows: 09:30–10:15 and 20:10–20:50 PST over the past two weeks. Sustained 95th QPS by route is in the attached sample column "q95_qps" (you have the file).
- Latency targets: We need P95 < 220ms and P99 < 600ms for customer-facing routes; internal batch routes can accept higher P99 up to 1.2s.
- Egress: We have a soft NIC cap of 3.2 Gbps and a monthly uplink budget with margin; sudden bursts are throttled at the edge by our network policy.

Two notes that affect sizing:
1) We have a short-lived traffic spike pattern every Monday at 09:00 when a scheduled job fans out requests for analysis — that is a ~7–10 minute surge and historically causes cold-cache penalties.
2) We can relax retention on some KV caches for non-critical tenants to speed warmup if needed.

We can be on the Friday slot at 10:30 PST for the playbook review. If you need the raw Prometheus export instead of the CSV, tell me and I’ll share a link.

—Alice
Senior SRE, Cobalt AI
[Attachment: none]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-17T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Cluster performance envelope & scaling playbook — initial traffic profiles

Thanks Alice — those numbers help. I pulled a quick sketch of a two-tier scaling approach and attached the draft playbook (scaling_playbook_draft.md). Key points summarized below:

- Traffic envelope mapping: map q50/q75/q95 to discrete pool sizes (N, 1.5N, 2N) where N equals the baseline GPU count for your average tenant mix. We recommend conservative step-ups for Monday fanout windows (+30% above q95) with a 10-minute warmup buffer.
- Warm pool strategy: keep a small warm pool (~5% of peak) with pinned KV cache snapshots to reduce cold-cache penalties for the Monday spike. Warm pool should live on the same VPC but on separate host groups to avoid noisy neighbor IO.
- Fast-fail path: if P99 exceeds 700ms despite scale-up, fallback to a compatibility model variant (smaller but lower latency) for premium routes, while routing noncritical requests to a lower-priority queue.

Jonas: can you validate the GPU-tiling and kernel warmup constants I used (I assumed 1.2s per model shard for cache population and 350ms tail per additional concurrent beam)? If those numbers look off we’ll adjust the warmup time and the step-up cadence.

Next steps:
- Jonas to run a Monte Carlo sim against Alice's CSV and return a recommended step ladder by EOD Thursday.
- Marissa to iterate scaling_playbook_draft.md and include explicit runbook commands and metrics to watch (queue depth, KV hit rate, NIC egress).
- Jordan to confirm Friday 10:30 PST and add the meeting invite.

Attachments: [Attachment: scaling_playbook_draft.md (MD, 12KB)]

Marissa Cole
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick turn, team. Confirming the agenda for Friday and capturing action items here so everyone has the same view: 

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Jonas Weber: run Monte Carlo sim on traffic_profile_v2.csv and output suggested pool sizes for q50/q75/q95 and Monday-fanout scenario — due 2026-11-19 EOD.
- Marissa Cole: finalize scaling_playbook_draft.md with runbook commands and fallback routing rules — due 2026-11-19 12:00.
- Alice Wu / Cobalt: confirm any enforceable egress throttles and whether you can pre-approve a short Monday-window burst exception (+10% NIC) — please reply by 2026-11-19 09:00.
- Jordan Blake: send calendar invite for Friday 2026-11-20 10:30 PST and include link to Drive doc; prepare a short slide with the performance envelope mapping.

Meeting objective: sign off on the traffic-to-pool mapping and have a signed-off runbook that operations can execute during Monday fanout — goal is to keep P99 < 600ms for customer routes while minimizing idle cost.

I’ll post the invite in 10 mins. If anyone prefers a pre-meeting dry-run we can do 20 minutes Thursday.

Thanks all,
Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
